source: Asset: branding/National Show 2027/Logo/NOS-2027-logo-full-colour-vertical.png, confirmed with Brad per team lead's dispatch (2026-09-11). Native pixel dimensions read directly from the PNG IHDR chunk (not assumed): 3272x2876px, aspect ratio (w/h) = 1.13769 -- i.e. very slightly wider than tall, despite the 'vertical' name (which distinguishes this lockup from a horizontal wordmark-beside-flower variant, not a literal portrait aspect ratio). Visually inspected (2026-09-11): a botanical illustration of a single orchid bloom above two lines of serif/mono text -- 'NATIONAL ORCHID SHOW' (tracked-caps serif, royal-purple ink) and, below a thin rule, 'WESTERN CAPE · 2027' (tracked-caps mono/sans, olive ink). No SAOC wordmark, no edition number ('19th'), no venue name, and no specific dates appear anywhere on the artwork.

reading.instruction: Brad: "replace the heading... with the actual vertical logo size to fit nicely in that heading space."
reading.ruling: FULL REPLACEMENT of the eyebrow ('The National Show') AND the serif lead-link heading ('19th SAOC National Orchid Show') with a single logo image. Both are folded into one visual unit today (a small mono caption directly above a serif link) and the logo image itself already carries the equivalent identity content ('National Orchid Show', plus 'Western Cape · 2027') -- keeping the eyebrow text as a separate sibling above the image would duplicate what the artwork already says and contradicts Brad's plain reading of 'replace the heading... with the logo', not 'add the logo above the heading'.
reading.metaLineRuling: KEEP leadMeta (venue name + formatted date range, rendered today via formatShowDateRange from the nationalShow Sanity singleton -- see MegaMenu.tsx's leadMeta computation) directly below the logo image, unchanged in its own rendering logic. Brad's instruction named only 'the heading' -- the logo does NOT carry the specific venue name (e.g. 'The Hangar, Stellenbosch Flying Club') or exact show dates, only the province and year, so dropping leadMeta would be a real information regression on the one piece of practical information ('where and when') a menu visitor is most likely to want. Do not remove it; do not fold it into alt text as a substitute for on-page text -- alt text is not a substitute for visible content per WCAG, and screen-reader users need leadMeta rendered exactly as sighted users see it.
reading.theShowGroupRuling: UNCHANGED. Brad's instruction addressed only the heading text, not the 'The Show' links list beneath it (Tickets / Show Sponsors / etc. leaves) -- no reading of his instruction extends to removing navigational leaves.

asset.note: branding/ is not a runtime-servable path (Next.js only serves /public) and is read-denied to agents by the autonomy floor per the team lead's dispatch note -- a specific named path happened to be readable when the architect verified dimensions directly (Read tool succeeded against the exact file above), but this does NOT establish it as copyable into public/. The team lead's own message says they will get it copied to public/images/ themselves; @dev must NOT attempt to read or copy the branding/ file -- treat public/images/nos-2027-logo-full-colour-vertical.png as a precondition dependency. If it is not present when @dev picks this up, STOP and report rather than reading from branding/ directly (see .claude/rules/scope.md -- branding/* is Brad's active design workstream, per project memory project_design_folders_brad_active).

containerBudget.computation: Grid track ratios (F7, unchanged): [1.05fr, 1fr, 1fr, 1fr, .9fr], sum 5. Outer wrapper: mx-auto max-w-[1280px] px-8 (32px each side) -> inner content width at >=1280px viewport = 1280 - 64 = 1216px. Lead track width = 1216 * (1.05/5) = 255.4px. Lead block's own padding-right (pr-6, 24px, unchanged from F7) leaves 231.4px of actual content width.
containerBudget.note: 200px image width (above) fits inside the 231px budget with an 11px margin against layout noise (sub-pixel `fr` rounding, borders) -- verified by real measurement in the e2e golden below, not assumed from this arithmetic alone. The image must NOT be styled at 100% of the track width (231px) with zero margin -- that leaves no breathing room and risks a 1-2px overflow into the Visit column's border-left at narrower-than-1440px real-world viewports.
